name: dongle
description: Connecting the Quest 3 directly with ethernet

blocks.text: **__Using an Ethernet-to-USB Dongle/Adapter on your Quest headset__**

It is possible to use a USB to Ethernet adapter or hub attached to your Quest 3 headset. While Meta has not stated any official support for this feature, they have been maintaining it and have fixed it when it was broken in the past.

**Steps:**

* Disable Wifi on your headset.
* Unplug your headset.
* Turn off your headset.
* Connect your Ethernet to USB adapter to your headset.
* Plug an Ethernet cable into your Ethernet to USB adapter and plug the other end into your router, hub, switch or PC (Must set up ICS for connecting directly to the PC with Ethernet. Type `/ics` in the channel for more information)
* Power on your headset.
* Open Virtual Desktop and connect to your PC.

**A few important points to know:**

1. This is not an officially supported feature and could possibly (but not likely) be removed by Meta at any time. (Meta removed this feature from the Quest 2 and the Quest 3 in the past but later restored it)
2. Many USB to Ethernet devices simply will not work. You'll need to research which ones will work. (Lots of documented working adapters listed here: https://discord.com/channels/564087419918483486/1390686127937159209 )
3. The headset will give you no indication that it's using the Ethernet connection other than that it simply works.

Note: Other headsets also support this connection method including Pico 4 Ultra, Play for Dream and GalaxyXR. The steps to use it on non-Meta headsets may be different than above.
